text: I had bilateral knee replacement surgery six months ago and was able to stand and walk within 24 hours. However, I needed a walker for about three weeks, then switched to crutches, and finally stopped using them in the third month. Initially, I had to take painkillers and anti-inflammatory medication, but I stopped in the third month because the pain lessened. I only experienced some stiffness at the surgical site and fatigue when walking or standing for long periods, as the surgical wounds needed time to heal. However, I could bend and straighten my legs immediately after the surgery and had good flexibility in movement. The doctor was pleased with my progress. Two and a half months later, I traveled back to my home country, using a wheelchair but no longer with crutches, and continued with physical therapy abroad to strengthen my muscles. Getting up, sitting down, and climbing stairs were the most time-consuming tasks, but by the fourth month I could do it, by the fifth month it was easier, and by the sixth month it was almost back to normal. I'm so happy to have regained my quality of life. With my knees free from pain and suffering from osteoarthritis, my mental state has also improved. Now I can walk normally, although I still need to be careful when climbing stairs. There's a little stiffness at the surgical site, but it's nothing to worry about. I'm incredibly grateful to the doctor for the best advice and treatment. When the doctor sees patients, he takes his time and listens attentively; he never makes you feel rushed. Anyone with chronic knee pain should consider this. I highly recommend consulting your doctor.

text:
We would like to express our sincere gratitude and appreciation to Dr. Warakorn for performing the Total Hip Replacement (THA) surgery on our Venerable Abbot.
Our Venerable Abbot had been experiencing AVN (Arthritis of the Joint) for over 10 years, with degenerative hip disease and increasing pain. Previously, he was not ready for surgery.
After consulting with Dr. Warakorn at his clinic, Dr. Warakorn recommended THA surgery, and our Venerable Abbot decided to proceed with the procedure.
Dr. Warakorn is highly skilled and experienced. The surgery was successful and safe. After the surgery, our Venerable Abbot (who is 81 years old this year) was able to walk within 24 hours. He experienced no pain and his post-operative recovery exceeded expectations.
There were no post-operative complications.
The pain has decreased.
Two weeks after the surgery, the wound was healed well. Dr. Warakorn explained the THA procedure using a model, clearly illustrating the process. He also provided excellent instructions on post-operative care, physical therapy, and muscle exercises for rehabilitation.
On behalf of the disciples, we extend our deepest gratitude to Dr. Warakorn for his invaluable care and surgery for our Venerable Abbot.
